headline: Stochastic and deterministic models of infection spread across host and population scales
label: Modeling Infection Dynamics Across Scales
summary: Recent preprints model stress-altered susceptibility, temperature-dependent Wolbachia infection loss, and superspreading tails in epidemic waves.
synthesis: The three preprints share a modeling strategy: mechanistic frameworks that connect infection or transmission processes to population-level outcomes under explicit environmental or host-state dependence. The aquatic study analyzes stress-driven susceptibility in both deterministic and stochastic formulations. An impulsive ODE framework models release strategies for Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti, in which temperature-driven infection loss is compared across the wMelPop, wMel and wAlbB strains. A Moyal-Poisson mixture model links individual-based stochastic SIR transmission to macroscopic pandemic waves and recovers superspreading in SARS. Stochasticity is central to two of the three studies, while environmental forcing is central to the aquatic and mosquito work. The new element in the epidemic framework is a distributional description that ties heavy-tailed wave structure to stochastic individual-level shocks.
